intro: France is one of the world's leading destinations for both international education and tourism, offering a rich cultural experience alongside a wide range of higher education opportunities. France has a distinctive higher education system that includes universities, Grandes Écoles, specialised schools and institutes.
why: Top-tier grandes écoles for business and management
Two-year job search permit after master's
Fashion, luxury and culinary programmes unmatched in Europe
visa: VLS-TS long-stay student visa via Campus France — Études en France registration, admission proof and €615/month funds evidence.
intakes: September is the main intake; January is available for many business programmes. Apply 8–10 months ahead.

req.label: Academics
req.value: 60%+ in bachelor's; GMAT/GRE for top business schools

req.label: French
req.value: B2 required for French-taught degrees; A1–A2 useful otherwise

req.label: Documents
req.value: Campus France registration, Marksheets, Resume, SOP, 2 LORs, transcripts, passport

sch.name: Eiffel Excellence Scholarship
sch.text: Monthly allowance plus travel and insurance for master's students

sch.name: Charpak Scholarship
sch.text: India-specific programme with tuition waiver and living support

steps.title: Register on Campus France
steps.text: Create your Études en France account and pay the fee

steps.title: Attend the interview
steps.text: Campus France academic interview at your regional office

steps.title: Accept admission
steps.text: Confirm the place and pay the tuition deposit

steps.title: Apply for VLS-TS
steps.text: Book the VFS appointment with funds and accommodation proof

steps.title: Validate on arrival
steps.text: Validate the long-stay visa online within three months

work: Students may work up to 20 hours a week. After a master's you can apply for the APS permit to stay two years and search for work, leading to the Talent Passport.
workPoints: 20 work hours permitted in a week

faq.q: Do I need to learn the French language to study in France?
faq.a: French proficiency is not required for English-taught programmes, but basic French can be helpful for part-time jobs and everyday life in France.

Yes — public tuition is a few thousand euros a year, far below business-school fees. Public universities generally charge tuition fees of a few thousand euros per year, making them more affordable than many private business schools.
